newsitem.title: USA: House passes $248 billion defense spending bill.
newsitem.headline: House passes $248 billion defense spending bill.

text.p: The House of Representatives passed on Tuesday a $248 billion defence bill that funds a 2.8 percent military pay raise and a range of "next-generation" military hardware.
The bill, which passed 322-105, also would halt spending for U.S. ground operations in Bosnia after June 30, 1998 unless Congress approves more money.
President Bill Clinton has threatened to veto the bill, which was $4.4 billion above his budget request and $3.9 billion above this year's spending.

The White House particularly objected to the threatened spending cutoff in Bosnia, saying that would "undercut our ability to complete successfully the NATO-led mission in Bosnia" which would "result in a serious loss of credibility with our allies, the Bosnian parties and with other countries participating in the Stabilisation Force."

The spending on military hardware would come at the expense of programmes that the Defence Department sees as higher priorities, and from an unacceptable shift of money from the Energy Department, the White House said.

But the House Appropriations Committee said the bill's funding is almost 1 percent below this year in inflation adjusted terms, and said the bill would produce the 13th straight annual decline in defence spending in real terms.
Overall, the bill would provide nearly $4 billion more than the administration wanted to buy hardware and equipment, and $770 million more for research and development programmes.
The bill would provide $505 million for B-2 bombers, a $331 million increase. The Defence Department has said the bombers cost more than they are worth.
It also would provide $3.67 billion -- $707 million above the White House request -- for missile defence programmes.
It also would fund Defence Department programmes dealing with Gulf War-related illnesses at $79 million, up 25 percent from this year's level.
The Senate earlier this month passed its $247 billion version of the bill.
